evidence_items.explanation: The experiments support the neural-generalization weakness in the contextual sense. They concern tested recurrent networks and task splits, not every neural architecture.

The study reports systematic generalization from a standard neural architecture trained through meta-learning, including comparisons with symbolic models. It materially qualifies the broad neural-versus-symbolic division without proving unrestricted neural generalization.

evidence_items.publisher: Journal of Artificial Intelligence Research; accepted manuscript on arXiv
evidence_items.locator: Section 8.1, discussion comparing neural program synthesis with inductive logic programming
evidence_items.explanation: The review describes symbolic methods that learn efficiently from examples, directly qualifying the claim that symbolic systems are poor at learning. It also identifies substantial practical limitations, so it does not establish symbolic superiority across learning tasks.
This critique argues that neural meta-learning successes depend on restricted task setups. It supports caution about broad generalization claims and limits how far e2 can be treated as a rebuttal.

unresolved_gaps: The evidence does not provide a common numerical comparison across all neural and symbolic methods.
The reach of neural meta-learning beyond its evaluated task families remains disputed.
No cited result establishes that symbolic systems generally transfer well when their representations or supplied rules are inappropriate.
